tagline: A whole analog vocal chain with pitch correction, a pitch shifter that keeps you sounding like you, and a visual EQ, voiced after famous records
description: Put it on a vocal and pick a record: Phil Collins' In The Air Tonight, Pharrell and SexyBack-era Timberlake, Travis Scott hard tune, 808s-era Kanye, Tame Impala, R&B, trip hop and more. Underneath is a full chain you can change: pitch correction (key, scale, retune speed, humanize, flex, formant), mic voicing, saturation, an eight-band dynamic EQ you drag on a live analyzer, a vocal rider, FET / opto / vintage-limiter / VCA compression, de-esser, a resonance smoother, air, doubler, chorus and Dimension, a vocoder that follows your voice, tape, tape delay, reverb and a true-peak limiter.
highlights: In The Air Tonight (Phil Collins, 1981): a dynamic mic into a cheap old limiter at 6:1 with a slow attack, almost dry with a dark tape echo, plus the vocoder version for the second verse

Pitch correction that keeps the voice natural: notes are moved whole periods at a time (PSOLA), so vowels and timbre stay put; retune speed from instant (the robotic effect) to gentle, humanize for held notes, flex for slides, natural vibrato kept or flattened

Pitch Shift: move your voice up or down by up to an octave and still sound like you, not a chipmunk (the formants stay where they are). A Formant knob sets the size of the voice on its own (younger and smaller, or bigger and deeper), and a pad shows where you are between natural and chipmunk

Visual EQ: eight bands you drag over a live analyzer of the voice before and after; each can be a bell, shelf, cut up to 48 dB/oct, notch, band-pass or tilt, on stereo, mid or side, and dynamic (it moves with the level in its band). Analog-matched curves stay true up to 20 kHz

Analog chain: mic voicing, tube / tape / console / crunch saturation (4x oversampled, tone, parallel mix), a vocal rider, and FET, opto, vintage-limiter or VCA compression with a sidechain filter and gain-reduction meter

Smooth (a resonance suppressor that tames harsh frequencies only while they ring), Air (mid and high air that stays smooth on esses), de-esser, doubler, chorus and Dimension widening, tape, a tape delay that ducks under the voice, plate / room / hall / chamber / gated reverbs and a true-peak limiter
Vocoder that plays the note you sing (and the chord of your key) with string, robot, choir or brass voices: no MIDI needed

45 presets, each a different record or job: DEON, 80s, 2000s, Travis Scott, Ye, Tame Impala, R&B, trip hop, moshc0re, studio essentials, pitched voices (including justend), INTERNET GIRL, neo soul and 60s soul
Favourites: star the presets you love and browse just those; your stars survive updates
installTips: Put Aircheck first on the vocal track (FL Studio: Mixer > vocal insert > slot 1; Ableton: the first device on the vocal track), then pick a preset.
For pitch correction set Key and Scale to the song; Chromatic works anywhere but snaps to every semitone. Retune 0 ms is the hard robotic effect, 20 to 50 ms sounds natural.

For a higher or lower voice use Pitch Shift: leave Formant at 0 and you still sound like you (turn Formant up with it only if you want the chipmunk). The PITCHED presets, including justend, start from there.
It delays the sound by about 60 ms so the pitch correction and Pitch Shift can look ahead; FL Studio and Ableton compensate automatically. To sing through it live, use a separate low-latency monitor.
previewNote: on a synthetic sung test phrase (slightly off pitch on purpose), so you hear the chain and the correction, not a real singer.

items: Uses about a quarter less CPU with exactly the same sound: the Mix knob's matching dry path only runs while Mix is below 100 %, and the resonance smoother skips its FFTs when it has nothing to take out

INTERNET GIRL presets (the Cape Town punk / hyperpop / trap trio): Distorted Lead (crunch preamp and a fast FET), Hyperpop Snap (hard tuning, up a tone, bright and doubled), Mumble Rap (warm, close, gently tuned, ducked echo)
Windows open at a size that fits your screen (about 80 % of a laptop's height) and can be dragged bigger; the size you pick is kept
Smoother windows: the static panels, shadows and grain are drawn once and reused, so meters and lights no longer redraw the whole window (3 to 4 times less drawing)
